hints: In parallelogram $ABCD$, opposite displacement vectors are equal; use $\vec{AD}=\vec{BC}$.
Find $\vec{BC}=\vec{OC}-\vec{OB}$, then add it to $\vec{OA}$ to obtain $\vec{OD}$.
walkthrough: In a parallelogram $ABCD$, the opposite vector displacements are equal, so $\vec{AD} = \vec{BC}$.

Find the vector displacement $\vec{BC}$ from position vectors $\vec{OB}$ and $\vec{OC}$:
$$\vec{BC} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 4 \\ -2 - 3 \\ -4 - 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ -5 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.Using Position Vectors: Derives a vector for one side, e.g. $\vec{AB}=(2,2,-1)$ or $\vec{BC}=(-1,-5,-6)$; Derives $\vec{OD}=\mathbf i-4\mathbf j-3\mathbf k$; Concludes with $\vec{OD}=(1,-4,-3)=\mathbf i-4\mathbf j-3\mathbf k$.

hints: Use $\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v=|\mathbf u||\mathbf v|\cos\theta$ for the directed sides $\vec{BA}$ and $\vec{BC}$.
Form $\vec{BA}=\vec{OA}-\vec{OB}$ and $\vec{BC}=\vec{OC}-\vec{OB}$ from the given position vectors.
Evaluate their scalar product and exact magnitudes before simplifying the quotient for $\cos\theta$.
walkthrough:
Identify the vectors that form the angle $\theta = \angle ABC$, which are $\vec{BA}$ and $\vec{BC}$ directed outwards from vertex $B$:
$$\vec{BA} = \vec{OA} - \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{BC} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ -5 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.Using Scalar Products: Evaluates the scalar product $\vec{BA}\cdot\vec{BC}=2+10-6$. Derives $2/\sqrt{62}$. Concludes with $\cos\theta=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{62}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{62}}{31}$.

hints: The area of the parallelogram is $|\vec{BA}|\,|\vec{BC}|\sin\theta$.
Use the exact cosine from part (b) with $\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta$; here $0<\theta<\pi$, so take the positive sine.
Substitute $|\vec{BA}|=3$ and $|\vec{BC}|=\sqrt{62}$, then simplify the surd into the form $p\sqrt q$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$ formed by vectors $\vec{BA}$ and $\vec{BC}$:
$$\text{Area} = |\vec{BA}||\vec{BC}|\sin\theta$$

Substitute $|\vec{BA}| = 3$, $|\vec{BC}| = \sqrt{62}$, and $\sin\theta$ into the area formula:
$$\text{Area} = 3 \cdot \sqrt{62} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{58}}{\sqrt{62}} = 3\sqrt{58}$$

Conclude with the exact area in the form $p\sqrt{q}$:
$$\text{Area} = 3\sqrt{58}$$

ai_rubric.Calculating Areas with Vector Products: Formation of $\sin\theta=\sqrt{58/62}$. Applies a area calculation, e.g. $2(\frac12|BA||BC|\sin\theta)$. The final result is $3\sqrt{58}$.
